# KLARA Public API documentation

> REST API for KLARA business software: accounting, finance, articles, customers, payroll and document delivery. Authentication with an API key or a bearer token. Every endpoint states the permission it requires and the KLARA roles that carry it.

## Machine-readable formats

- [OpenAPI specification](https://developer.klara.ch/klara-openapi.json): the contract, 98 operations, OpenAPI 3.0.3
- [Build information](https://developer.klara.ch/build-info.json): when this was built and from which source

## Endpoint reference

Each file lists the operations of one area with parameters, request and response bodies, and the permission each operation needs.

- [Accounting](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-accounting.md): 24 operations
- [Accounting Interface](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-accounting-interface.md): 1 operation
- [Article](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-article.md): 28 operations
- [Authentication](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-authentication.md): 3 operations
- [Company](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-company.md): 3 operations
- [Company documents](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-company-documents.md): 1 operation
- [Company general](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-company-general.md): 4 operations
- [Customer](https://developer.klara.ch/md/reference-customer.md): 14 operations

## Notes for agents

- The HTML page and these files are generated from one source in the same build. Where they disagree, the OpenAPI specification is the contract.
- Every guide file names its canonical page, so a citation can point a human at the same content.
- There is no test environment for KLARA. Every call goes to production, so treat writing calls as chargeable and irreversible.
- The rate limit is counted per calling IP address, not per API key.
- Most operations require exactly one permission. Do not infer a permission from a path; each operation states its own.
